tasks.name: Develop Leaderboard UI

tasks.name: Test Leaderboard Functionality

T1.implementation_approach: Design a user-friendly interface with search, filter, and categorization options for problems.
T1.notes: Ensure responsive design for compatibility across devices.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle CRUD operations for problems.
T2.notes: Focus on scalability and secure data handling.

T3.implementation_approach: Set up database schema and establish connections with the backend using an ORM.

T4.implementation_approach: Create an interactive code editor with syntax highlighting and auto-completion features.
T4.notes: Use libraries like CodeMirror or Monaco Editor.

T5.implementation_approach: Build a backend service to compile and execute code securely in isolated environments.
T5.notes: Implement sandboxing to prevent malicious code execution.

T6.implementation_approach: Connect the code editor UI with the compiler backend via API calls.
T6.notes: Ensure real-time feedback and error handling.

T7.implementation_approach: Design a profile page to display user details, activity, and achievements.

T8.implementation_approach: Develop backend APIs to manage user data and authentication.
T8.notes: Ensure secure password storage and session management.

T9.implementation_approach: Set up a database schema to store user profile information.
T9.notes: Ensure data normalization and indexing for efficient queries.

T10.implementation_approach: Design a leaderboard UI to display top users with sorting and filtering options.
T10.notes: Focus on a visually appealing and intuitive layout.

T11.implementation_approach: Develop backend APIs to calculate and fetch leaderboard rankings.
T11.notes: Optimize ranking calculations for large datasets.

T12.implementation_approach: Integrate the leaderboard backend with the database to fetch and update rankings.
T12.notes: Ensure real-time updates for leaderboard changes.

T13.implementation_approach: Create a UI to display hints and solutions for problems in a collapsible format.
T13.notes: Ensure hints are accessible without revealing full solutions.

T14.implementation_approach: Develop backend APIs to manage hints and solutions for each problem.
T14.notes: Implement access control to restrict unauthorized access.

T15.implementation_approach: Perform end-to-end testing of problem repository features, including UI and backend.
T15.notes: Use automated testing tools for efficiency.

T16.implementation_approach: Test the integration between the code editor and compiler for various programming languages.
T16.notes: Simulate edge cases and handle errors gracefully.

T17.implementation_approach: Validate user profile functionality, including data updates and authentication.
T17.notes: Test for security vulnerabilities like unauthorized access.

T18.implementation_approach: Test leaderboard functionality for accurate ranking and real-time updates.
T18.notes: Simulate high traffic to ensure performance under load.

T19.implementation_approach: Verify the display and functionality of hints and solutions for problems.
T19.notes: Ensure proper access control and UI responsiveness.

T20.implementation_approach: Deploy the application to a production environment with proper CI/CD pipelines.
T20.notes: Monitor performance and address any post-deployment issues.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize SQLAlchemy instance
db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    tags = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=True)  # Comma-separated tags
    input_format = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    output_format = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    example_input = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)
    example_output = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Problem {self.title}>'

from app.database import db
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, Boolean

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = Column(String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = Column(String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = Column(String(128), nullable=False)
    is_active = Column(Boolean, default=True)
    problems_solved = relationship('Problem', backref='solver', lazy=True)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.username}>'

from app.database import db
from app.models.problem import Problem
from app.models.user import User

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now(), nullable=False)

    # Foreign key to associate with a User
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    user = db.relationship('User', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))

    # Foreign key to associate with a Problem
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    problem = db.relationship('Problem', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Solution id={self.id}, user_id={self.user_id}, problem_id={self.problem_id}, language={self.language}>"

from flask import Blueprint, request, jsonify, render_template
from app.database import db
from app.models.solution import Solution
from app.models.problem import Problem
from app.models.user import User

solution_bp = Blueprint('solution', __name__)

@solution_bp.route('/solutions', methods=['GET'])
def list_solutions():
    """
    Endpoint to list all solutions in the database.
    """
    solutions = Solution.query.all()
    return jsonify([{
        'id': solution.id,
        'code': solution.code,
        'language': solution.language,
        'user_id': solution.user_id,
        'problem_id': solution.problem_id
    } for solution in solutions])

@solution_bp.route('/solution/<int:solution_id>', methods=['GET'])
def view_solution(solution_id):
    """
    Endpoint to view a specific solution by ID.
    """
    solution = Solution.query.get(solution_id)
    if not solution:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Solution not found'}), 404
    return jsonify({
        'id': solution.id,
        'code': solution.code,
        'language': solution.language,
        'user_id': solution.user_id,
        'problem_id': solution.problem_id
    })

@solution_bp.route('/solution/new', methods=['POST'])
def create_solution():
    """
    Endpoint to create a new solution.
    """
    data = request.json
    code = data.get('code')
    language = data.get('language')
    user_id = data.get('user_id')
    problem_id = data.get('problem_id')

    # Validate user and problem existence
    user = User.query.get(user_id)
    problem = Problem.query.get(problem_id)
    if not user or not problem:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Invalid user or problem ID'}), 400

    # Create and save new solution
    solution = Solution(code=code, language=language, user_id=user_id, problem_id=problem_id)
    db.session.add(solution)
    db.session.commit()

    return jsonify({'message': 'Solution created', 'solution_id': solution.id}), 201

@solution_bp.route('/solution/<int:solution_id>/edit', methods=['PUT'])
def edit_solution(solution_id):
    """
    Endpoint to edit an existing solution.
    """
    solution = Solution.query.get(solution_id)
    if not solution:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Solution not found'}), 404

    data = request.json
    solution.code = data.get('code', solution.code)
    solution.language = data.get('language', solution.language)
    db.session.commit()

    return jsonify({'message': 'Solution updated', 'solution_id': solution.id})

@solution_bp.route('/solution/<int:solution_id>/delete', methods=['DELETE'])
def delete_solution(solution_id):
    """
    Endpoint to delete a solution by ID.
    """
    solution = Solution.query.get(solution_id)
    if not solution:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Solution not found'}), 404

    db.session.delete(solution)
    db.session.commit()

    return jsonify({'message': 'Solution deleted'})

from flask import Blueprint
from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_bp
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_bp
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_bp

def register_routes(app):
    """
    Registers all blueprints for the application.
    """
    app.register_blueprint(problem_bp)
    app.register_blueprint(user_bp)
    app.register_blueprint(solution_bp)

from flask import Flask, render_template
from app.database import db
from app.routes import register_routes

def create_app():
    # Initialize the Flask app
    app = Flask(__name__, template_folder='../templates', static_folder='../static', static_url_path='/static')

    # Configure the app (example, replace with actual config as needed)
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///acm_platform.db'
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False

    # Initialize the database
    db.init_app(app)

    # Register routes and blueprints
    register_routes(app)

    # Create database tables
    with app.app_context():
        db.create_all()

    # Define the home route
    @app.route('/')
    def home():
        return render_template('index.html')

    return app

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A web application designed to help users solve ACM-style competitive programming problems.

## Features

- Problem Repository: A comprehensive library of ACM-style problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Editor: An integrated code editor with syntax highlighting and support for multiple programming languages.
- Online Compiler: A feature to compile and run code submissions directly on the platform.
- User Profiles: Personalized user profiles to track progress, solved problems, and rankings.
- Leaderboard: A ranking system to display top users based on problem-solving performance.
- Hints and Solutions: Optional hints and detailed solutions for problems to aid learning.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
